name: Île-de-France
summary_text: Île-de-France sits fractionally below the national 0.67, but the deviation is small because the negative and positive factors largely cancel for a traveller. On the negative side, the Paris agglomeration and urban units over 200,000 inhabitants concentrate 55% of anti-LGBT offences for 43% of the population—a rate of 9 per 100,000, more than double the rural 4 (2025 update: 54% for 43%, still 9 per 100,000 against the rural 4 and national 7). The 2025 Marche des Fiertés was mobilised under a heavy police frame; the self-declared "gay patriot" collective Eros sought to march with prefectural backing, Inter-LGBT threatened to cancel if it participated, and participants reported that "the Marche des fiertés is becoming a sensitive event." A visitor attending the Pride encounters organisational tension and a security apparatus that signals vulnerability even as it protects. On the positive side, the 9-per-100k rate is heavily inflated by reporting propensity, community visibility, dedicated police liaison desks and the density of associations—all of which mean more incidents are recorded and responded to, not necessarily that a visitor is at greater risk; Paris alone records 22 per 100,000 but the official note cautions that offences there also involve non-residents (commuters and tourists). Île-de-France has the country's densest trans support infrastructure and the largest community, giving a discovered visitor the best odds of institutional help and social buffer anywhere in metropolitan France. Net deviation: −0.02 from national. The dossier's own caveat is explicit: "high recorded rates in Paris should not be read as Paris being dangerous." Compare with Bourgogne-Franche-Comté (0.62), where the state actively banned assembly; Île-de-France's state response to Pride was protective if tense. Compare with PACA (0.65), which shares the metro-rate exposure but adds the Fréjus dress-code incident as a specific negative on public appearance.

sources.claim_summary: Interior-ministry statistics service (SSMSI) Infraction rapide n°53, May 2025: 4,800 recorded anti-LGBT+ offences in France in 2024 (+5% on 2023; crimes/délicts up 14%/year since 2016); only about 4% of victims file complaints; acts concentrate in urban units over 200,000 inhabitants, notably Paris — whose rate, 22 per 100,000 against the national 7, the note attributes partly to non-resident victims and commuters; recorded victims are >70% men.
